Messages.Author: Daniel Frey
Messages.Body:
By now most of us know how to construct a gangrel deck or a malkavian
deck. Some deck construction is pretty straight forward and as soon as
you know which clan you wish to play you just pull the necessary cards.
I'm curious to hear peoples stories creating original, funny and/or
sometimes pointless decks. All start with a couple of examples to
explain my meaning.

A friend of mine made a drunken riot deck. Brujah with a bunch a loyal
street gangs, arsons and a distraction or two. He chose the cards by the
illustrations. If it had looting, rioting or general drunkeness in the
graphic it was part of the deck. It didn't do much but was funny to
watch.

Somebody posted somewhere about a deck where two vamps would have
shotguns, one would bum's rush get a shot off, press and earth meld to
end combat and untap. The other one would hidden lurker and start combat
again, do the same as above, keep doing it until the job was done.
Seemed highly uneffective.

My own addition was actually workable (I've only played it once, I was
very lucky and cleared a table). Bring out Masika and a bunch of
Toreodor blockers. Give Masika aching beautys- two or three are best.
Play a clan impersonation to...Malkavian. This will get their attention.
Follow it with a Malkavian Madness Network. Masika then gets to bleed,
untap between peoples turns and bleed at the end of their turn. You're
able to get off between 8+ bleed/turn in a four person game.
It has a very lengthy set-up time and of course every resource must be
used to keep the Madness network in play and keep Masika alive. (This is
the only deck that I've felt justified in playing a fistful of Majesty)

I would love to hear other people's concepts and ideas.

I once made a "Mad Masika's Harem" based around Masika, two copies of Talbot's
chainsaw, and all the Malkavians with celerity, auspex, and obfuscate.
The goal of the deck was to get Masika out with a sport bike, the Rack, a
hunting ground, and an obfuscate card, then block someone, and Disguised
Weapon the Chainsaw and go to work. I had some other weapons in there in
case the primary combo didn't work.

It was an okay deck, and I've played it a bunch around here, so people are
someone scared of it. The amusing thing about the deck is that it only wins
if I don't bring out Masika until the endgame. Its a fine Malk/Torie
intercept deck, but the blood cost of its primary purpose is just too high.

I've been having some fun with a concept in the JOL games. The nice thing
about JOL is that you can have as many of those obscure rares that you
want in a deck.

The concept:
Temptation,
Heidelburg Castle.

I have tried this concept with a FOS deck but the FOS really have limited
combat defence. I am forced to rely on Majesties which a true combat deck
thrashes. On the other hand, I can tempt those annoying combat monsters and
abuse them royally. What I do is tempt, wait a few turns, take control and
take an action, then use HC to xfer all blood and equipment to one of my
minions. Now the poor sap has to hunt (unless he has a HG) and I get control
again next turn. By including costly cards in my deck the vampire is MINE,
MINE, all MINE!!! All he gets to do is hunt. If he has a HG out or a blood
doll, there are some easy solutions if you know what I mean. (Think
day op, RTI, 6+ bleeds with stealth, Arson, etc.). Heck, with Antidiluvian
Awakenings, once you tempt the guy, you can just about guarentee that he is
going to be burnt or some other decent vampire.

Once I get 2 or 3 temptations on my prey, I really, really mess with his
game. The problems are that the deck is slow to develop, pitiful on defense,
and once I ouste my prey I lose some of MY borrowed minions and have to start
all over again. But even when I lose it is such fun to wreak havoc by stealing
his minions, Mind Numbing his remaining defender, and blitzing his depleted
lines.

Because I am tired of my poor Settites having to cower in hidden corners, I
am now trying to build a similar deck around Suhailah. With superior Fortitude
for combat survival and Prince for intercept it should do a little better.
Saqqaf also has fortitude and a few skill cards should provide a meeting of
clans. But this deck is still pretty raw and I made some big mistakes in my
current version.

The basic idea behind the deck is to make voting as painful as possible.
Then, I try to make the other Meths WANT to vote.
I'll play Malkavian Seven Miseries, Bureaucratic Overload, princes,
the Elysiums, etc. to cause general disarray. It's heavy on the Malkavian
game cards (Game of Malkav, Malkavian Time Auction, Malkavian Prank).
It's not always very effective, but it's fun as hell. Yes, I have won with
the
deck before.
One of my favorite stunts is to play Malkavian Rider Clause, followed up
with Command of the Harpies. "The proposer of said document hereby
promises to go on a much-needed vacation."

Another idea for a deck I'll try at a later date is the Turkish Bazaar
deck.
It's an Assamite deck that sells Contracts and other cards to other Meths
using the Succubus Club. I'll probably throw in a number of clan-specific
cards and Clan Impersonations for enterprising Meths (like myself, in a
small market).

vampires with D actions, placing ambush/Bum's Rush cards with a few good
weapons, say .44's, several Haven uncovered cards, then go to town of the
other players. This deck did clear the table once, but it is mostly just

Another good deck is the "machine bleed" I use vampires with superior

and you are ready to bleed with "Force of will" until your vampire runs

mods and your prey is out.

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
herr...@gold.tc.umn.edu (Christian S Herro) writes:
>Speaking of which, could someone remind me what exactly the complete rule
>on no repeat actions is?

From the DCI:

1. Repeat Action rule: No single vampire can repeat an action in a turn.
This refers to the particular action type. For example, a vampire which
successfully bleeds its prey via Computer Hacking, then untaps via Freak
Drive, cannot perform any bleeding action again whatsoever that turn,
regardless of whether or not it is a Computer Hacking action.

>1. Repeat Action rule: No single vampire can repeat an >action in a turn.

What exactly is an action type? Is it only an action that duplicates one
of the basic actions (e.g. all the D bleeds), or does it include cards
that have the same basic effect but are different? (For example,
presumably Bum's Rush and itself are the same action type, but what about

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
JlB1925 (jlb...@aol.com) wrote:
: >1. Repeat Action rule: No single vampire can repeat an >action in a turn.

: > This refers to the particular action type.
: What exactly is an action type? Is it only an action that duplicates one
: of the basic actions (e.g. all the D bleeds), or does it include cards
: that have the same basic effect but are different? (For example,
: presumably Bum's Rush and itself are the same action type, but what about
: a Rush and an Ambush, or a Rush and a Haven action?)

An action type is any type of action defined by the rulebook:
* Bleed
* Hunt
* Employ (Retainer)
* Recruit (Ally)
* Equip (incl. transferring equipment)
* Call a vote
* Leave Torpor
* Rescue (from Torpor)
* Diablerize (in Torpor)

Additionally, each action card (by name) that is used to take
an action not listed above is its own type (by name).

And, each card in play that provides an action not listed
above is its own type (by name).

Bum's Rush, Ambush, and the attack allowed by a Haven Uncovered
are all different types of actions.

--
L. Scott Johnson (vte...@regency.wizards.com)
Official VtES Net.Rep for Wizards of the Coast.
(*) - Subject to review by Rules Team

The confusion here is due to the fact that unlike some other cards (i.e.
Bum's Rush, Albative Skin) GtU qualifies as a "Type" of action (it is
listed as a category of action in the rulebook). In the case of GtU,
there are two reasons (category of action and card name) that prevent it
from being repeated.

While I see your point that this is a "bleed" action (the category) and
the superior version is not a "bleed" action, both are still "Govern the
Unaligned" actions and prevented by the card name restriction.

Robert

Messages.Author: James Hamblin
Messages.Body:
Robert Goudie wrote:
>
> The confusion here is due to the fact that unlike some other cards (i.e.
> Bum's Rush, Albative Skin) GtU qualifies as a "Type" of action (it is
> listed as a category of action in the rulebook). In the case of GtU,
> there are two reasons (category of action and card name) that prevent it
> from being repeated.

Every specific card is its own type of action. So, for example, you
couldn't Bum's Rush twice in a turn anymore than you can Govern the
Unaligned twice in a turn. People get confused because infGtU and
supGtU are actions which do different things, but they are both "Govern
the Unaligned". So you can Bum's Rush _and_ Ambush in the same turn
becuase "attack" isn't an action type and they are two different cards.

Just hoping to clear things up...

The No Repeat Actions rule extends the restriction used by
cards like Change of Target and Obedience. And these cards'
restriction has already been ruled to treat actions as the
same by card name. In the same way that Eagle's Sight inferior
and superior are the same action modifier, for purposes of
that restriction.
